verdict.rationale: Foreloop lets a non-engineer start work from a plain-language problem statement without knowing which files change. After a person approves the contract, an agent claims the task, does the work and opens a pull request, so implementation can happen without a traditional engineering handoff. However, the evidence never describes taking a mockup or design file as input; the only visual inputs are user-feedback screenshots. The agent also has to be run by someone in a repository checkout on their own machine, which is a technical setup step. Missing for 10: design/mockup ingestion, a PM-operable flow that needs no local agent setup, independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a product-manager, I can go from a mockup or design to a working implementation without an engineering handoff

citations.quote: "Users can't tell which invoices are overdue" is enough to start; you do not need to know which files change.
That agent asks Foreloop for approved tasks in that repository, claims one, does the work, and opens a pull request from your GitHub account.
Nothing runs until a person approves a contract. Approval is the only gate
The agent then checks Foreloop for approved tasks on a cadence and works them as they arrive.
The widget adds the page, its metadata, and an optional screenshot, so the model fixes the right thing.
